newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-TAYLOR SURVIVES TENSE FINAL SESSION.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TAYLOR SURVIVES TENSE FINAL SESSION.

text.p: Mark Taylor, his captaincy under growing threat after a series of low scores, survived a last, tense 80 minutes as Australia struggled in their three-day match against Gloucestershire on Wednesday.

Taylor was unbeaten on 19 as Australia, trailing by 101 on the first innings, were 43 without loss in their second innings at the end of the second day of their three-day match against the current county championship leaders.
Gloucester opener Nick Trainor was largely responsible for home side's comfortable first innings lead, scoring 121, his maiden first-class century.
Trainer hit 17 fours in his 246-ball innings and shared a third wicket partnership of 142 in 34 overs with Rob Cunliffe who made 61.
Leg-spinner Shane Warne topped the bowling figures with four for 97 and Michael Kasprowicz took three for 101.
Taylor was still clearly out of touch when Australia batted again and at one stage went 11 overs without scoring. But he at least survived to fight another day.
